newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Monsanto sees rise in 1997 investments.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Monsanto sees rise in 1997 investments.

text.p: Monsanto Co, which spent an additional $350 million in 1996 for new businesses, product development and other investments, expects to spend even more this year.
"Clearly this kind of spending will increase again in 1997," Monsanto Chief Economist Nicholas Filippello said in an interview on Thursday.
He said much of the 1997 spending had been earmarked for agricultural operations, an area in which Monsanto has been developing enhanced crops and making key acquisitions.

Monsanto said its investments for acquisitions, research spending, major product developments, new product launches and other growth initiatives rose by about $350 million pretax in 1996 compared with 1995 expenditures.
While Filippello declined to provide a specific figure, he said 1996 spending was "in the neighborhood of $900 million."

In 1997, the company expects to close its proposed $240 million acquisition of Asgrow Agronomics, a unit of Mexico's Empresas La Moderna SA de CV, and its planned purchases of Holden's Foundation Seed Co, Corn States Hybrid Service and Corn States International for a total of $1.0 billion.
Asked about future acquisitions, Filippello said, "We will continue to look for opportunities that help us to build that growth platform."
Development costs for 1997 also will cover drugs in the pipeline of the G.D. Searle pharmaceutical unit.

Monsanto said the "growth investments" trimmed $150 million from its 1996 net income. Earlier Friday, it reported 1996 earnings of $885.0 million, up from $728.0 million the previous year, both excluding extraordinary items.
"What we're trying to do is strike a balance between continued growth in near-term financial performance at the same time we're building a very strong foundation for future growth," Filippello said.
In a step toward building that foundation, Monsanto plans to spin off of its chemical operations, a deal the company hopes to complete by late summer.
In the fourth quarter, Monsanto's chemical operations recorded a pretax operating profit, excluding extraordinary items, of $82.0 million, up from $78.0 million a year ago.
The Searle pharmaceutical unit's adjusted pretax income rose to $56.0 million in the fourth quarter from $35 million in the year-earlier period.
Food ingredients' adjusted pretax operating earnings rose to $64.0 million from $62.0 million.

Agricultural operations, which typically suffer losses in the fourth quarter because of seasonal factors, showed an adjusted pretax loss of $48.0 million, compared with an adjusted loss of $47 million in the year-ago period.
